## What it costs to buy this home

Buying in Sweden adds about 1.5-3.5% in taxes and fees on top of the price: roughly €1,365 to €3,185 here, so plan for about €92,365 to €94,185 in total.

Stamp duty on the title (lagfart) of 1.5% of the price or tax value, whichever is higher, plus a SEK 825 fee; if you borrow and need new mortgage deeds (pantbrev), 2% of their amount plus a SEK 375 fee; optional legal advice; the seller normally pays the agent, and a cooperative flat (bostadsrätt) has no lagfart.

Every year: Houses pay a municipal property fee (kommunal fastighetsavgift) of SEK 10,425 in 2026, or 0.75% of the tax value if that is lower.

General information, not tax advice: ask a local lawyer or notary for the exact figure.

## What it costs to buy this home

Buying in Poland adds about 2.5-4% in taxes and fees on top of the price: roughly €1,822 to €2,915 here, so plan for about €74,707 to €75,800 in total.

Tax on civil law transactions (PCC) 2% of the value, paid by the buyer within 14 days of the deed; notary fee (taksa notarialna) capped at PLN 1,010 plus 0.4% of the value above PLN 60,000, plus 23% VAT; court fee of PLN 200 to enter ownership in the land register (plus PLN 100 for a new register); optional lawyer about 1%; the agent fee (about 2-3%) depends on the agreement.

Every year: Owners pay a local property tax (podatek od nieruchomości) set by the commune, capped in 2026 at PLN 1.25 per m² of usable floor space for flats and houses.
